summary: The work is real and mostly sound. I independently re-ran everything: migration 235 applies cleanly to a fresh scratch DB I built myself (fh_t10_verify, cloned from fundhub_t10_base, dropped after — never fundhub_ci, never production); the table lands with RLS ENABLED + FORCED + a named policy (verified in pg_class/pg_policies), affiliate_id nullable, a non-blank code check, and both indexes. src/http/routes.test.mjs 15/15 pass, affiliate-click.pg.test.mjs 10/10, affiliate-stats.pg.test.mjs 8/8. No existing migration was edited (git diff --name-only db/migrations is empty). No -intended.md touched. docs/END-TO-END-VERIFICATION.md untouched — no drive-by. No new outbound fetch() in any Unit A file. No raw IP or raw user agent reaches a column (the INSERT binds only hashes, and hashIp returns null with no salt — proven by test). No existing test was modified, skipped, deleted or .only'd. node --check passes on all five .mjs files. The HTML is whole, not half-wiped: affiliate.html grew 640 to 799 lines and the div count went from 102 open / 103 close (genuinely broken, as claimed) to 110/110. Every declared marker string is present. THE MONEY RULE HOLDS: there is no COALESCE(commission_due, 0) anywhere; an unrated conversion is counted as converted while commission_due stays NULL, and the pg test asserts strictEqual(commission_due, null). What fails is honesty-of-the-screen. The screen now shows TWO DIFFERENT conversion rates for the same data — the CONVERTED tile says "44% of 9 tracked" while the funnel bar directly below says "33% of referred", visible together in the agent's own evidence screenshot. The funnel divides by total referred, which includes referrals whose conversion state is admittedly unknown, so it reports a lower rate as fact and contradicts the tile. That is one line to fix. Secondary: the CONVERTED tile paints a hard number even when zero referrals are tracked, and by the agent's own blocker no referral on the platform ever reaches 'converted', so CONVERTED is structurally 0 for everyone — a measurement-shaped zero. Also flagged: an unindexed Seq Scan over clients per affiliate row (EXPLAIN confirmed) that a 200-row staff roster read will multiply, and the fact that the only UI evidence is a fixture render (the screenshot header reads "NO DB"), not the real app.

violations.what: The same screen reports two contradictory conversion rates for the same data. paintFunnel computes the Converted bar's caption as converted/referred, but the CONVERTED tile computes converted/(referred - untracked). With the agent's own fixture (12 referred, 3 untracked, 4 converted) the tile reads '44% of 9 tracked' and the funnel bar 12 lines below reads '33% of referred'. The funnel's denominator includes the 3 referrals whose conversion state the endpoint explicitly reports as UNKNOWN via referred_untracked, so 33% is an understatement presented as a measured fact. An affiliate sees both numbers at once and cannot tell which is true. Fix is one line: use the tracked denominator in paintFunnel, or drop the percentage from the funnel entirely.
violations.evidence: Code: sub: (converted !== null && referred) ? Math.round((converted / referred) * 100) + "% of referred" : ""  --- vs tile at line ~640: var tracked = referred - untracked; note = Math.round((converted / tracked) * 100) + "% of " + tracked + " tracked". Rendered proof in the unit's own evidence: docs/workflows/fix-2026-08-18/evidence/T10/A-affiliate-counting/affiliate-tiles-and-funnel-after.png shows CONVERTED tile '44% of 9 tracked' and REFERRAL FUNNEL converted bar '33% of referred' on one page.

violations.what: CONVERTED paints a hard number where the truth is unknown. When every referral is untracked (referred > 0, untracked === referred), converted_count is 0 and the tile prints '0' with the caption 'no tracked referrals yet'. The big number is the thing a non-reader sees. By this unit's OWN declared blocker — af-02 never writes an affiliate_referrals row, so no referral anywhere ever reaches 'converted' — CONVERTED is structurally 0 for every affiliate on the platform. That is a zero produced by a broken pipeline being displayed as a measurement, which is the exact failure mode the previous em dash avoided. The dash was replaced with a number that is not measured.
violations.evidence: if (converted === null || referred === null) { set("kConv", "—"); ... } else { set("kConv", String(converted)); var tracked = referred - untracked; var note = tracked > 0 ? ... : "no tracked referrals yet"; ... }  — there is no branch that returns to the dash when tracked === 0. Manifest blocker text: "no referral anywhere ever reaches 'converted'".

violations.check: 12 DID IT ACTUALLY DO THE JOB — performance of the fix
violations.what: The REFERRED lateral does a full sequential scan of the clients table once per affiliate row returned. There is no index on upper(btrim(custom_fields->>'affiliate_tier1_owner')) — I listed every index on clients and none covers the expression. readHandler caps limit at MAX_LIMIT = 200, so a staff roster read triggers up to 201 full scans of clients in one request. An affiliate's own read filters to one row and is fine; the owner/finance roster is the risk. Recommend a CREATE INDEX on the expression before this ships.
violations.evidence: EXPLAIN on my scratch DB: 'Nested Loop Left Join -> Seq Scan on affiliates a (rows=200) -> ... -> Seq Scan on clients c  Filter: ((org_id = a.org_id) AND (upper(btrim((custom_fields ->> 'affiliate_tier1_owner'::text))) = upper(a.tracking_id)))'. \di clients* returns only clients_pkey, clients_org_email_uniq, clients_org_client_code_uniq, clients_client_master_key_key, clients_partner_idx, clients_is_demo_org_idx.

violations.what: There IS a COALESCE on a money column: COALESCE(SUM(l.amount), 0) AS paid_total. I checked whether this turns unknown into zero and it does NOT — this is the acceptable case, reported for the record rather than as a defect. affiliate_payout_lines.amount is 'numeric(14,2) NOT NULL' (033_affiliates.sql:519), so the SUM is only NULL when there are zero settled lines, which genuinely means zero dollars left. The unit also returns paid_runs so the screen can say 'no payout run has settled yet' instead of a bare $0, and it does. Critically, commission_due is NEVER coalesced anywhere in this change — I grepped the whole diff. NOT a violation, but the orchestrator should see that the pattern was found and adjudicated.
violations.evidence: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(l.amount), 0) AS paid_total FROM affiliate_payouts p JOIN affiliate_payout_lines l ...  |  033_affiliates.sql:519  amount        numeric(14,2) NOT NULL  |  pg test asserts strictEqual(stored.commission_due, null) — the NULL survives to the row.

violations.what: Two client-side '|| 0' fallbacks collapse an unknown count to zero, in the same file whose own comment forbids exactly that. If referred_untracked ever arrived null, untracked becomes 0, tracked becomes the full referred count, and the CONVERTED rate would be computed over a denominator that silently includes unknowns while claiming to be 'tracked'. Same for unrated_converted_count, whose zero would suppress the 'N with no rate set' caption and the OWED caveat — i.e. a missing value would hide the money-is-unknown warning. Unreachable today because COUNT(*) never returns NULL, but it is the precise defaulting the num() helper was written three lines earlier to prevent.
violations.evidence: var untracked = num(mine.referred_untracked) || 0;  and  var unrated = num(mine.unrated_converted_count) || 0;  — directly beneath the comment 'Nothing here defaults a missing count to zero.' on the num() helper at line 500.

violations.check: 12 DID IT ACTUALLY DO THE JOB — counting correctness
violations.what: A client can be double-counted across two affiliates. The referred lateral unions affiliate_referrals rows for affiliate A with any client in the org whose custom_fields code matches A's tracking_id, de-duplicating only WITHIN one affiliate. If a client's attribution was corrected — the referral row credits affiliate B while custom_fields still carries A's old code — that client counts toward A's referred_count AND B's referred_count, and is reported to A as 'untracked'. 033 enforces one direct referral row per client via ON CONFLICT (client_id, tier) DO NOTHING, so the structured side is unique; the custom_fields side has no such guard. Not fabricated data, but REFERRED can overstate after any manual attribution change.
violations.evidence: UNION ALL SELECT c.id, false FROM clients c WHERE c.org_id = a.org_id AND a.tracking_id IS NOT NULL AND upper(btrim(c.custom_fields->>'affiliate_tier1_owner')) = upper(a.tracking_id)  — no NOT EXISTS guard against a referral row crediting a different affiliate.

violations.what: Both new pg suites carry mutable state between tests inside one describe, so several assertions are true only because of execution order. In affiliate-click.pg.test.mjs the 'unknown code' test asserts rows.length === 1 for DEAD_CODE, but the 'does not leak' test two tests later posts DEAD_CODE again. In affiliate-stats.pg.test.mjs the CLICKS test opens by asserting clicks_count === 0, which only holds because no earlier test inserted a click. Correct today under node:test's serial-within-describe execution and both suites pass on a re-run, but they will fail confusingly if ever reordered or run concurrently. Not a weakened test — the assertions are real and would fail against the old code.
violations.evidence: assert.equal(rows.length, 1, "a dead code is a fact worth keeping, not a discard");  followed at line ~105 by  const fake = await post({ ref: DEAD_CODE });

violations.what: The only UI evidence for a UI change is a fixture render, not the real screen. CLAUDE.md §6 point 4 requires a Playwright check on any UI change. The screenshot's own header badge reads 'NO DB', and NOTES.md states the page was 'rendered against a fixture that returns one affiliate row'. The server side is genuinely proven — I re-ran both pg suites against a real Postgres and they pass through the real netlify/functions/api.mjs front door — but the tiles have never been seen painting a response from the live endpoint. The fixture also cannot exercise the tracked === 0 case flagged above.
